rationale: This quantitative empirical study (2006-2010 household- and child-level survey data in Peru using an IV strategy) examines household/municipal water service provision under communal/cooperative utility governance (Comités Vecinales and Juntas Administrativas de Servicios de Saneamiento, instrumented via municipal personnel resources and administrative urban/rural classification; keywords include 'water utilities, cooperatives, child health, regulation, Peru'). Criteria 1, 2 (both narrow utility-ownership/regulatory-structure and plain institutional/governance), and 3 are satisfied. However, the title and abstract report only child health ('diarrhea among under- five year old children') as the outcome; full-text retrieval is required to determine whether intermediate or secondary water service-access outcomes (such as household connection, coverage, continuity, chlorination/service quality, or affordability) are also empirically analysed (Criterion 4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: No divergence between the narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings: communal/cooperative utility ownership and regulatory structure (Comités Vecinales and JASS versus public/private utilities, alongside administrative urban/rural municipal classification) satisfies both the narrow utility-ownership/regulatory-structure reading and the plain institutional/governance reading. Under both readings, the Phase 5 decision is 'unsure' because the abstract explicitly reports child diarrhea (health) rather than direct water-access metrics, requiring full-text inspection to verify Criterion 4.

evidence_quotes.quote: we investigate the effects of communal water provison (Comités Vecinales and Juntas Administrativas de Servicios de Saneamiento) on child health in Peru.
Using detailed survey data at the household- and child-level for the years 2006-2010, we exploit the cross-section variability to assess the differential impact of this form of provision.
The results show a negative and signi cant effect of comunal water provision on diarrhea among under- five year old children.
